purpose: Test a delay-robust LQR fallback within the unchanged LQR+PPO+gain architecture, after previous parameter-only study failed.
preserved: same signed dynamic bicycle plant and vehicle magnitudes
LQR plus bounded scalar PPO residual
changed: LQR Q/R tuned only on validation with fixed-delay linear stability eligibility
actor initialization to known fast-LQR prior using existing ReLU units, with same initial total decision for PPO baseline
same explicit reward and randomized training as preceding study
test_conditions: four known reference families x three delay regimes plus two DLC mass perturbations=14; fresh parameters/seeds; not unseen-family zero-shot.
selection: LQR fallback gain chosen before all new training using validation only. All three final PPO checkpoints reported; no best-seed choice or per-scenario switching. Test runs after all training.
baselines: Include both the matched robust LQR fallback and the original fast LQR; unchanged declared MPC20 and equal-budget/equal-prior trained PPO. No superiority over optimally tuned MPC is claimed.
hypothesis: Robust fallback can improve delay completion; low-delay PPO may recover tracking precision. Every-scenario rank1 is a target, not a promised conclusion.
